query: Why do habits break, and how do you make one hold?
why_in_two_sentences: The top organic results for this query are two academic papers, not consumer guides: the ScienceDirect review shows only its highlights and abstract on the page (judged as such), and Bouton's PMC paper reviews why behavior change fails to sustain. Neither offers a lay reader any procedure, while ours gives the interruption mechanics, the order of operations, and 34 FAQs; the papers' only edge is the named, cited science our relapse sections assert without referencing.
what_we_do_that_they_dont: Turns the mechanism into an executable procedure: find the exact two seconds, interrupt the body position, focus, or self-talk, then install the replacement
Explains why one bad day undoes three good weeks and why the habit returns at the same time of day, in reader language
34 verbatim FAQs including the 21-day rule, the habit loop, habit stacking, and specific habits (vaping, night eating, skin picking)
Separates habit from addiction and routes clinical cases to professionals up front

above_the_fold.ours: H1 is the query, the short answer names the three-part sequence (body position, focus, sentence) and the interrupt-first order, then recognition sentences; immediately actionable.
above_the_fold.theirs: ScienceDirect shows highlights bullets on the two-system model (stimulus-driven vs goal-directed); credible and dense, but unusable as guidance for someone trying to stop doing something tonight.

questions_they_answer_that_we_dont: Why does the habit come back when I go back to the place where I used to do it?
trust_signals: Both competitors are peer-reviewed papers with DOIs, author affiliations, and reference lists; ours asserts the same mechanisms (relapse, context effects) with zero citations.
one_change_with_most_traffic_impact: Name and cite the extinction research inside the relapse sections (change is not erasure; the old pattern resurges under stress and in old contexts), converting our strongest sections from assertion to evidence at near-zero cost.
